meaning.consistent-with-label-carbon13: sits above an allowed mass by a whole number of carbon13 labels (1.0034 Da each), which is what a carbon13-labelled ion or its M+1 isotope peak looks like; declare the standard's label count to have the filter accept it
meaning.consistent-with-label-deuterium: sits above an allowed mass by a whole number of deuterium labels (1.0063 Da each), which is what a deuterium-labelled ion or its M+1 isotope peak looks like; declare the standard's label count to have the filter accept it
meaning.consistent-with-label-nitrogen15: sits above an allowed mass by a whole number of nitrogen15 labels (0.9970 Da each), which is what a nitrogen15-labelled ion or its M+1 isotope peak looks like; declare the standard's label count to have the filter accept it
meaning.legal-within-100mDa: an allowed mass exists within 100 mDa, so this ion falls in a gap that makes the model discriminating rather than broken
meaning.legal-within-10mDa: an allowed mass exists within 10 mDa, so this ion falls in a gap that makes the model discriminating rather than broken
meaning.legal-within-300mDa: an allowed mass exists within 300 mDa, so this ion falls in a gap that makes the model discriminating rather than broken
meaning.legal-within-30mDa: an allowed mass exists within 30 mDa, so this ion falls in a gap that makes the model discriminating rather than broken
meaning.legal-within-5mDa: an allowed mass exists within 5 mDa, so this ion falls in a gap that makes the model discriminating rather than broken
meaning.nearest-legal-above: m/z of the closest allowed mass, which lies above this ion
meaning.nearest-legal-below: m/z of the closest allowed mass, which lies below this ion
meaning.needs-halogen-alphabet: possible only if the halogen alphabet (Cl, F, Br, I) is allowed; the default model excludes it
meaning.no-legal-ion-nearby: no mass allowed by the selected model lies within 400 mDa of this ion
meaning.possible-as-doubly-charged: explainable as a doubly charged ion (z=2); the deployed model assumes z=1

notes: A reason code is something this build of the filter actually checked. Codes are per peak and several can apply at once. 'strong' codes name a chemistry the caller could declare to change the verdict; the others only state a distance. Above table_max_mz nothing is ever reported impossible: the tables say possible for every mass there, so a removal that high is a fault, not a verdict.
